title: Release v0.5.0
description: Integrate the completed PIM API improvements, update the README for the release, bump the crate, run all release gates, and verify GitHub, crates.io, and Homebrew publication.
acceptance_criteria: README clearly summarizes the v0.5.0 API improvements; main contains the API work; local CI-equivalent checks pass; v0.5.0 is published with both macOS tarballs; crates.io and the Homebrew tap expose v0.5.0; main is clean and pushed.
close_reason: Released v0.5.0 from green main commit 5390f14. GitHub release is published with both macOS tarballs; crates.io and the shared Homebrew tap serve 0.5.0; README and release notes document the API improvements; local and remote gates passed.

title: Deepen core PIM APIs and stable identity contracts
description: Finish stable identifier targeting across Calendar and Mail; replace the shallow handwritten schema with complete declarative command metadata; add batch operations with structured partial results; deepen Calendar, Mail, Contacts, and Reminders APIs; add deterministic contract tests; and add prompt-free auth-status plus a cider doctor command. Preserve compact JSON, envelopes, dry runs, the public Rust library, and the existing fast SQLite read paths.
design: Keep Cider as a single Rust binary/library. Do not add a public backend selector or Swift/Node sidecars in this pass. Prefer additive output fields, ID-only destructive targeting, one subprocess per batch, explicit partial-failure results, and prompt-free diagnostics.
acceptance_criteria: Calendar and Mail mutations use stable identifiers rather than title/date or list indexes; schema describes every command/action and is covered by drift tests; supported Calendar/Reminders/Mail batch operations execute in one subprocess and return per-item results; Calendar/Mail/Contacts/Reminders gain the prioritized missing read/write fields and verbs; auth-status and doctor are prompt-free; compact JSON/envelope/dry-run contracts remain valid; cargo fmt, clippy including no-default-features, tests, release build, representative CLI QA, commit, and push all pass.
close_reason: Implemented stable Calendar/Mail/Contacts/Reminders identity contracts, parser-derived complete schema, prompt-free doctor/auth-status, batch operations with partial results, richer core PIM fields/verbs, compatibility aliases, docs, tests, performance checks, and all quality gates.

title: Review and enable marketplace plugins
description:
The following plugin marketplaces have been configured for this project:

- beads-marketplace
- allbeads-marketplace
- claude-plugins-official-marketplace
- claude-code-marketplace
- skills-marketplace
- chrome-devtools-mcp-marketplace
- claude-skill-marketplace
- repomix-marketplace
- prose-marketplace

Consider which plugins would be useful for your workflow and enable them:

```bash
# List available plugins
claude plugin marketplace list

# Enable a plugin
claude plugin enable <plugin>@<marketplace>
```

Note: beads and allbeads plugins are enabled by default.
